title: TP/TE for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
context_label: High-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia after EMA/CO
schedule_label: Day 1 is paclitaxel and cisplatin. Day 15 is paclitaxel and etoposide. One full cycle lasts 28 days.
schedule_summary: Paclitaxel runs over three hours, followed by cisplatin and kidney-protecting fluids. Anti-sickness medicines are stronger at this visit. After paclitaxel, etoposide runs over an hour. Your team checks for infusion reactions. Treatment is usually planned for two to four complete 28-day cycles, guided by hCG and tolerance.
purpose: Treat the trophoblastic tumour with the aim of cure. Serial blood hCG measures how the disease responds.
indication_text: For high-risk GTN resistant to or recurring after EMA/CO.
administration_text: Paclitaxel runs over three hours, followed by cisplatin and kidney-protecting fluids. Anti-sickness medicines are stronger at this visit. After paclitaxel, etoposide runs over an hour. Your team checks for infusion reactions. Treatment is usually planned for two to four complete 28-day cycles, guided by hCG and tolerance.
monitoring_summary: Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests. Check serum hCG on day 1, more often if indicated.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Prevents tumour cells completing cell division.
agents.mechanism: Prevents tumour cells completing cell division.
agents.watch: Report numbness between visits and tell the nurse at once about chest tightness during treatment.
visual: Prevents tumour cells completing cell division.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.
agents.mechanism: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.
agents.watch: Attend for fluids and blood tests. Report hearing changes or reduced urine.
visual: Links strands of DNA together so tumour cells cannot divide normally.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.mechanism: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse if you feel faint or breathless during the infusion.
visual: Prevents tumour cells repairing DNA during division.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Paclitaxel
serious_effects.text: Tell your team if tingling affects walking or using your hands.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Paclitaxel
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, tightness or breathlessness.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report ringing in the ears or trouble hearing conversation.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report reduced urine, vomiting or difficulty drinking.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report numb fingers, tingling or difficulty with buttons.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for fever, chills or unexplained bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Infusion reaction · Etoposide
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, faintness or breathing problems.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: Day 1 is paclitaxel and cisplatin. Day 15 is paclitaxel and etoposide. One full cycle lasts 28 days.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills or sudden illness. Report new tingling or hearing changes before your next infusion. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest tightness or breathing difficulty.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Report any numbness, hearing changes and previous infusion reactions.
After remission your specialist arranges hCG every two weeks for six months, then monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.

questions.q: Why should I report tingling or ringing in my ears before the next visit?
questions.a: Paclitaxel is given at both visits. Cisplatin is given on day 1 and can affect hearing and nerves. Tell your team about ringing, changes in hearing, numb fingers or difficulty fastening buttons so they can check which medicine needs review.

evidence.title: Paclitaxel-based salvage treatment in GTN
evidence.interpretation: A specialist series reports activity with alternating paclitaxel-based doublets in relapsed or resistant GTN.
evidence.limitations: Small non-randomised cohort. Prior platinum exposure and individual response affect interpretation.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before treatment
cells: Check blood count, kidney and liver tests, serum hCG and ECG. Assess renal clearance and hearing when indicated.
Report any numbness, hearing changes and previous infusion reactions.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests. Check serum hCG on day 1, more often if indicated.
Ask how your hCG trend affects the next treatment.

rows.label: After treatment
cells: Continue follow-up through your GTN service.
After remission your specialist arranges hCG every two weeks for six months, then monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.

monitoring_schedule.note: Scan dates and tumour-marker testing are individualised by your oncology team.
